children: New Delhi, Nov. 18 -- Anil Agarwal, the Chairman of Vedanta, has claimed that the government's decision to transfer operations of a producing offshore oil and gas block from his company to state-run Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) could send a wrong signal to investors.
"Recently, our running field has been given to ONGC, which will send a very wrong signal to investors," Agarwal said in a post on LinkedIn.
Agarwal said Vedanta Oil and Gas was committing USD 5 billion to scale up production to between 300,000 and 500,000 barrels per day.
The company produced about 72,200 barrels of oil and oil equivalent gas in the July-September quarter, according to its regulatory filing.
Agarwal said India is on the verge of a major oil and gas opportunity, comparable to Guyana's emergence as a significant hydrocarbon province a decade ago.
Vedanta Oil and Gas had also entered the deepwater Samudra Manthan programme, he said.

"We are seeing such great energy and enthusiasm from global investors. This is the time to keep the policy hand steady and not disrupt any existing operator. That shall go a long way in building and boosting global investor confidence," Agarwal said.
"Let us all together make a determined move to increase domestic production and reduce oil and gas imports drastically," he added.

The remarks come against the backdrop of an ongoing legal dispute over the CB-OS-02 Cambay offshore block, where Vedanta held a 40 per cent participating interest, ONGC 50 per cent and Invenire Petrodyne the remaining 10 per cent.

The production-sharing contract for the block expired on June 29, 2023. Vedanta and its joint venture partners had applied for an extension on June 28, 2021, under the government's 2017 extension policy. But the government declined the request through a September 19, 2025 communication and directed the operator to hand over the block to ONGC.

Vedanta challenged the decision before the Delhi High Court on September 22, 2025. The company's writ petition was dismissed on July 22, 2026, resulting in the vacation of an interim stay that had earlier directed status quo to be maintained. ONGC subsequently took over the block and applied for a petroleum lease on July 28, 2026.

The legal dispute, however, remains unresolved. Vedanta appealed against the single-judge order before a division bench of the Delhi High Court. Hearings have concluded, and the judgment has been reserved, according to the two companies' filings.

Vedanta recognised an impairment charge of approximately Rs.379 crore in the first quarter of FY27 against assets and receivables associated with the block, citing the absence of a valid production-sharing contract and uncertainty over their recoverability. The company also stopped recognising revenue and related expenses from the block from July 22.

title: 'Very wrong signal to investors': Anil Agarwal on transfer of Vedanta's oil and gas block in Gujarat to ONGC
